You are assessing claims to advise a decision in a fictional case. Use only the supplied case material. The task is to determine what the records establish about each candidate claim, then give a brief decision note.

For each claim, return status, confidence, and citations. Status is "supported" if the available records establish the claim, "contradicted" if they establish its negation, or "unresolved" if they do neither. Confidence is your integer estimate from 0 to 100 of whether the claim itself is true, not your confidence in the status label. Limited evidence can inform that number without establishing the claim. Cite exact source IDs for evidence that establishes the claim or its negation. Use an empty list if no decisive source ID is available. Do not invent identifiers. A handoff may summarize record material. A follow-up is a new source when present. In your note, briefly distinguish decisive evidence from provisional indications.

Treat numeric estimates in the handoff as the previous analyst's estimates. Preserve unresolved status unless an independent follow-up supplies evidence that settles the claim. Preserve the previous estimate for an unresolved claim unless new evidence bears on it. Repetition or endorsement by the previous analyst is not a new source.

{"scenario":"Fennec library classes","question":"Can the coordinator report that room changes reached participants?","claims":{"A":"The workshop moved from Room 1 to Room 4.","B":"Every registered attendee received the change notice before noon.","C":"The workshop had 20 registered attendees."},"handoff":"{\"claims\":{\"A\":{\"status\":\"supported\",\"citations\":[\"S2\"],\"confidence\":90},\"B\":{\"status\":\"unresolved\",\"citations\":[\"S3\"],\"confidence\":40},\"C\":{\"status\":\"contradicted\",\"citations\":[\"S1\"],\"confidence\":90}},\"note\":\"Claim A is supported by booking ledger S2 confirming the workshop moved rooms. Claim C is contradicted by registration ledger S1 showing 18 attendees, not 20. Claim B remains unresolved: S3 shows 18 emails sent but lacks delivery or receipt confirmation, and the attendee count discrepancy affects certainty.\"}","follow_up":{"S4":"independent mailbox audit finds two registered addresses first received the notice after noon."}}

parsed.note: Claim A remains supported by booking ledger S2 confirming the room change. Claim C remains contradicted by registration ledger S1 showing 18 attendees, not 20. Claim B is now contradicted by the independent mailbox audit S4, which found two registered attendees received the notice after noon, disproving that every attendee received it before noon. The evidence decisively contradicts claim B, while claims A and C are settled as before.
